Hi Alex / Sam,

Thanks again for joining the demo today — really enjoyed hearing about the FinWave use cases (real-time risk summarization + customer support triage). Below is a concise recap and recommended next steps so we can get a focused eval set up.

Recap (what we heard)
- Real-time summarization of trade narratives at ~350 tokens per request with a tight 200-300ms p99 SLA
- High throughput bursts during market open (50-150 qps) and lower steady-state otherwise
- Priorities: latency + cost predictability; acceptable small quality delta for most summaries but not for regulatory narratives

Model & quantization recommendations
- Start with a 7B-13B open model variant we validated for summarization latency/cost (see attached trade-study).
- Run a two-path eval: AWQ (8-bit aware quant) for the lowest cost baseline, GPTQ (4/8-bit) for a middle ground, and FP8 for highest fidelity low-latency requirements.
- We'll provide a prompt set (attached) with regulatory and non-regulatory examples so you can see quality deltas.

Next steps
1) Rishi (cc'd) will provision a dedicated eval instance and share the benchmark link + brief instructions.
2) Please upload any sensitive prompt examples (redacted) to the shared Drive link so we can include them in the eval.
3) We'll run the AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade-study using your prompt set and report token-cost, latency p50/p99, and qualitative regression notes within 4 business days.

Attachments: redwood-quant-trade-study-v1.pdf (trade study template), finwave-prompt-set-v1.txt (initial prompt set)

If that sounds good I'll have Rishi kick off the provisioning.

Hi all — quick notes from a 50-sample eval run (attached short report + artifacts). High-level:

- FP8 vs fp16: FP8 preserves fidelity closest to fp16 in our benchmarks for summarization and regulatory texts; measured QA pass-rate delta vs fp16 was ~0.4% on the sample set. Recommendation: use FP8 for regulatory flows when latency demand is strict; otherwise fp16 is safest if you can't accept any regression.

- AWQ behavior: AWQ (8-bit aware quant) keeps KV cache semantics intact; warm-up latency is equivalent to fp16 in our infra because Redwood's runtime materializes the cache similarly across quant modes. Multi-request conversational behavior should be preserved.

- AWQ vs GPTQ cost delta (13B): on average tokens served: AWQ ~= 0.55x cost of fp16; GPTQ (more aggressive 4-bit where applicable) ~= 0.35x cost of fp16 but show higher variance in QA metrics for safety-critical prompts (we saw a ~1.8% regression on the 50-sample regulatory subset).

Attachments: redwood-quant-trade-study-v1.pdf (filled with 50-sample numbers), quick-qual-notes.txt

Proposed next steps:
1) Provision two eval instances: AWQ-13B and FP8-13B (we can add GPTQ if you want to push cost further but recommend gating on the regulatory subset results).
2) Run a full 500-sample sweep across their redacted prompt set and report token-cost, latency p50/p99, and QA regression per quant mode (3 business days).

If you give the go-ahead I'll start provisioning and share an ephemeral access link + benchmark dashboard.

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
